items.justification: Secure development practice and API abuse controls address different attack surfaces.
Publishing a support period and supporting users through an incident share no objective beyond both being supplier duties.
Both pursue identification of security risks across the lifecycle; A by continuous monitoring of fielded products, B by assessment triggered on configuration change.
Both require development artefacts to be tracked and auditable; A through version control, B through a documented audit trail of models, datasets and prompts.
Both require a documented justification when a security expectation cannot be met; A for absent updates, B for poorly secured components.
Automatic update activation and recovery is unrelated to asset tracking and version control processes.
Development-time practice and runtime monitoring of internal model states pursue different objectives.
Patching quickly and re-testing after a major update are distinct duties that together make update handling secure.
A restricts disclosure of security information to unauthenticated parties; B mandates disclosure of data handling to users. Opposite directions, different objectives.
Both give users actionable security information; A guidance for checking secure state, B threat descriptions with recommended actions.
Both mandate secure deletion of data; A on user request, B at decommissioning, each specifying obligations the other omits.
Making components updateable and publishing hashes so updates can be authenticated are distinct halves of secure software distribution.
User guidance on secure setup is unrelated to internal asset tracking and version control processes.
Both address remediation of vulnerabilities in fielded products; A the monitoring and rectification, B the provision and delivery of the resulting patches.
Minimizing interface information disclosure and communicating threats to stakeholders pursue different objectives.
Input validation prevents manipulation through the interface; protecting training data from unauthorized access is a different control.
Key lifecycle management and the security content of system documentation share no objective.
Securely managing sensitive parameters and maintaining an auditable lifecycle record of assets combine into one asset governance control.
Both concern getting security updates to users; A the user's control over installation, B the supplier chain that delivers them.
Transport cryptography and asset version control processes pursue different objectives.
Secure development processes and least-privilege permissions between systems are unrelated controls.
Cryptographic verification of an update and notification of the user about it are distinct steps of one secure update process.
Recording justifications for unmet recommendations is unrelated to supporting users through an incident.
Providing updates and verifying them on receipt are distinct obligations on different parties within one secure update chain.
Both require accessible security guidance to users; A at setup, B when updates are released.
Development process requirements and runtime performance monitoring pursue different objectives.
Data erasure instructions and update notifications are different obligations sharing only the user-communication channel.
A addresses the end user; B addresses internal staff awareness. Different audiences and objectives.
Both require accessible documentation to users about the product; A the sensing capabilities, B the guidance for use and configuration.
Communications cryptography and threat communication to stakeholders share no objective.
Following secure development processes and risk-assessing externally sourced components are distinct parts of one development assurance control.
Pre-build risk assessment and post-release vulnerability monitoring are distinct stages of lifecycle risk management.
Publishing a disclosure policy for external reporters is unrelated to internal staff threat-awareness training.
Publishing a support period and justifying the use of an undocumented component pursue different objectives.
Notifying users of a required update differs from the developer's duty to re-test after a major version change.
Releasing fixes promptly and testing releases before shipping are distinct duties in one secure release process.
Both defend against reverse engineering of an interface: A by keeping credentials out of the binary, B by limiting abuse of the exposed API.
Update activation and recovery is unrelated to monitoring model behaviour drift.
Checking for available updates is unrelated to verifying that specified security controls were implemented.
Vulnerability monitoring by the supplier and contractual flow-down to cloud providers do not combine into a single nameable control.
